// (64..65, 6, 12) under the aisle). Hay stacks flank a 2-wide aisle that runs from the ladder foot to the loft door
// at z9; lanterns stand on the hay tops and on the barrels. Written into air only, through layers().

const LANTERN = ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }];
const BARREL = ["barrel", { facing: "up" }];

export function build(g) {
  const origin = [62, 7, 10];
  const legend = {
    h: "hay_block",
    b: BARREL,
    L: LANTERN,
  };
  // y7: stacks x62..63 and x66..67 (z10..12), barrels at the back east corner (66..67, z14)

  return layers(g, origin, legend, [
    [
      "hh..hh",
      "hh..hh",
      "hh..hh",
      "......",
      "....bb",
    ],
    [
      "hh..hh",
      "hh..hh",
      "hh..hh",
      "......",
      "....LL",
    ],
    [
      "L...L.",
      "......",
      "......",
      "......",
      "......",
    ],
  ]);
}

// P5 barn aisle and stalls (room box x62..67, y1..5, z10..14). Drawn as text with layers(): one legend, one slice per
// storey of the room. The centre aisle x64..65 stays clear from the front doors (z9) to the back doors (z15); the four
// mule stalls stand either side of it, their fronts on the aisle (x63 / x66) with open gates at z11 and z13. The loft
// ladder at (62, 1..5, 14) is built by the stair joiner, so that cell is left as it is ('.' in the text).
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  const legend = {
    H: "hay_block", // feed rack at the stall head
    B: ["barrel", { facing: "up" }], // water trough
    P: "spruce_fence", // stall front post
    W: ["spruce_fence", { east: "true", west: "true" }], // partition between the pens (z12)
    G: ["spruce_fence_gate", { facing: "east", open: "true" }], // gate on the west stalls' aisle side
    g: ["spruce_fence_gate", { facing: "west", open: "true" }], // gate on the east stalls' aisle side
    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }], // hangs from the loft floor (y6)
  };

  // y1: stalls, racks, troughs, gates (x62 back, x63 aisle front; x66 aisle front, x67 back)
  layers(g, [62, 1, 10], legend, [
    "HP..PH",
    "BG..gB",
    "WW..WW",
    "HG..gB",
    ".P..PH",
  ]);

  // y2: the partition fences rise to shoulder height
  layers(g, [62, 2, 10], legend, [
    "......",
    "......",
    "WW..WW",
    "......",
    "......",
  ]);

  // y5: hanging lanterns under the loft floor, off the hay drop hole at (64..65, 6, 12)
  layers(g, [62, 5, 10], legend, [
    "..L...",
    "......",
    ".L..L.",
    "......",
    "...L..",
  ]);
}

input.summary:
Part room-34 (P5 hay loft) now writes nothing: its hay stacks, barrels and lanterns all sit on cells Shell B and the roof already built, so the 26 refused writes were duplicates, not conflicts.
make.sh runs clean with `room: P5 hay loft: 0 placed`, no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE, and produces build.nbt (exit 0).
The part's comment now records that Shell B's hay_stack owns the loft stacks; the hay loft's light is still unresolved (see left).
left: The hay loft is dark: `mcd light --rooms rooms.json --only "P5 hay loft"` gives min 0, mean 6.7, 9 dim cells and 2 DARK cells, against the plan's floor light of 8 or more. The part's only lanterns were the refused ones, so the loft needs lanterns placed in free air cells by a fitting or furnisher part.

The barn loft's ownership is unclear: Shell B builds the hay stacks at y7..8 and the roof builds the upper air at y9, while room-34's layout assumed the stacks and lanterns were its own. The owner of the loft fit-out (shell_b or room-34) should be decided before anyone re-adds content here.
make.sh's REFUSED list is truncated to 8 of 26 cells in its output; the full list is only in parts-report.json.

waste.what: Worked out which of the 30 wanted cells were already occupied by hand: dumped the built grid cell by cell with a throwaway script (three tries to get the block-name accessor right) and cross-checked the refusal sample against shell_b.mjs's hay_stack calls.
waste.cost: About 7 tool calls, one dump script, 3 greps; the refusal output shows only 8 of 26 cells, the rest is in parts-report.json.
waste.tool: A `mcd occupancy <build> --part "room: P5 hay loft"` (or runParts printing each refused write with the owning part's name and the occupant block) would have named Shell B as the owner in one line.

waste.what: The `placed N` count is wrong: layers() increments its counter for every g.set attempt, and runParts refuses silently, so the report said `placed 4` for a part that placed nothing.
waste.cost: One source read of layers() to confirm the count was counting attempts; a misleading number that cost a reasoning step.
waste.tool: runParts should count accepted writes only (placed = attempted - refused), or layers() should return the guard's accepted count.

waste.what: No check that a part's light survives its own edit: the loft's only lanterns were refused, and I found the dark loft only after the fix, by running `mcd light` by hand.
waste.cost: One extra mcd light call after the fix; the regression was invisible to make.sh, which reports only refusals and palette.
waste.tool: A per-part `mcd light --only <room>` line in the runParts log (or a room-light gate in build.mjs) would flag the dark room at the part that lost its light.

companions.task: Plan the hay loft's light: free air cells at y7..11 x62..67 z10..14 for lanterns (hung from the roof soffit or standing on the hay tops if the cells are free), so the floor reads 8 or more and no cell is dark.
Decide who owns the loft fit-out (Shell B's hay_stack at y7..8 against room-34's old layout) and confirm the hay stack layout, so the loft is not built twice.
